knowledge_point.title: Finding a General Solution in Implicit Form

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{\left(x+5\right)}}{\sqrt{\left(y+4\right)}}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\sqrt{\left(x+5\right)}}{\sqrt{\left(y+4\right)}} \\ \sqrt{\left(y+4\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\sqrt{\left(x+5\right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \sqrt{\left(y+4\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \sqrt{\left(x+5\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ \int \sqrt{\left(y+4\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int \sqrt{\left(x+5\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ \int {\left(y+4\right)}^{1/2}\,\text{d}y & =\int {\left(x+5\right)}^{1/2}\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{2{\left(y+4\right)}^{3/2}}{3} & =\frac{2{\left(x+5\right)}^{3/2}}{3}+K \\ {\left(y+4\right)}^{3/2} & ={\left(x+5\right)}^{3/2}+C \\ \sqrt{{\left(y+4\right)}^{3}} & =\sqrt{{\left(x+5\right)}^{3}}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=\frac{3K}{2}.$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\sqrt{{\left(y+4\right)}^{3}}=\sqrt{{\left(x+5\right)}^{3}}+C.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2x}{{e}^{\left(y+5\right)}}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2x}{{e}^{\left(y+5\right)}} \\ {e}^{\left(y+5\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {e}^{\left(y+5\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{\left(y+5\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{\left(y+5\right)}\,\text{d}y & =\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\ {e}^{\left(y+5\right)} & ={x}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
{e}^{\left(y+5\right)}={x}^{2}+C.
$$

generation.domain: all real x,y; right side plus C>0

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\sqrt{1-{\left(y-2\right)}^{2}}\,$ for $\,|\left(y-2\right)|<1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\sqrt{1-{\left(y-2\right)}^{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{\left(y-2\right)}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{\left(y-2\right)}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{\left(y-2\right)}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{\left(y-2\right)}^{2}}}\,\text{d}y & =\int \text{d}x \\ \operatorname{arcsin}⁡\left(y-2\right) & =x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\operatorname{arcsin}⁡\left(y-2\right)=x+C.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{{sec}^{2}⁡\left(y+1\right)}$ for $-\frac{\pi }{2}<\left(y+1\right)<\frac{\pi }{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{{sec}^{2}⁡\left(y+1\right)} \\ {sec}^{2}⁡\left(y+1\right)\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {sec}^{2}⁡\left(y+1\right)\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int 1\,\text{d}x \\ \int {sec}^{2}⁡\left(y+1\right)\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int 1\,\text{d}x \\ \int {sec}^{2}⁡\left(y+1\right)\,\text{d}y & =\int 1\,\text{d}x \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡\left(y+1\right) & =x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\left(y+1\right)=x+C.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\left(x+5\right)}{{e}^{\left(y-6\right)}}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2\left(x+5\right)}{{e}^{\left(y-6\right)}} \\ {e}^{\left(y-6\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2\left(x+5\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {e}^{\left(y-6\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int 2\left(x+5\right)\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{\left(y-6\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int 2\left(x+5\right)\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{\left(y-6\right)}\,\text{d}y & =\int 2\left(x+5\right)\,\text{d}x \\ {e}^{\left(y-6\right)} & ={\left(x+5\right)}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
{e}^{\left(y-6\right)}={\left(x+5\right)}^{2}+C.
$$

generation.domain: all real x,y; right side plus C>0
